s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pelvic pain with abdominal mass and recent aggravation
salient_findings: 10 cm mass palpable in pelvic cavity, fixed to anterior rectum
Hard texture and significant tenderness of the mass
Multiple nodules in pelvic area on MRI and CT
key_facts: 40-year-old woman with 8-year history of right lower abdominal pain
Recent aggravation of pain and abdominal expansion sensation
Surgical history includes multiple procedures for fibroids and ovarian cysts
Patient has a 2-year smoking history but quit 5 years ago
Abdomen is soft and tender in lower part without rebound tenderness
Pelvic examination reveals a fixed mass with clear boundary and limited mobility
Rectal examination shows a hard, mobile, non-tender mass 7 cm from anus
CA125 level is 35.08 U/ml
Hormone levels are LH 44.87 IU/L, FSH 108.8 IU/L, Prolactin 6.62 μg/L, Progesterone 0.16 ng/mL, Estradiol <15 pg/ml, Testosterone 12.08 ng/dL
Biopsy results show smooth muscle tumor
Immunohistochemistry is positive for CD34, SMA, desmin, focal CD10, ER, PR, and 2% Ki-67

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Smooth muscle tumor with high Ki-67 index and recent aggravation of symptoms

shortlist.label: Uterine carcinosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple surgeries for fibroids and ovarian cysts, and presence of a large pelvic mass

shortlist.label: Ovarian cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA125 level and presence of a large pelvic mass

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD34 and presence of a large pelvic mass

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large pelvic mass with clear boundary and limited mobility, and history of multiple surgeries for fibroids and ovarian cysts

raw.rationale: The patient's history of multiple surgeries for fibroids, the presence of a fixed mass with clear boundary and limited mobility, and the biopsy results showing a smooth muscle tumor with positive immunohistochemistry for CD34, SMA, desmin, and ER/PR support the diagnosis of leiomyosarcoma.

rejected.label: Uterine carcinosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient has undergone total abdominal hysterectomy, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Ovarian cancer
rejected.why: The CA125 level is not significantly elevated, and the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: The immunohistochemistry results are negative for CD117 and Dog-1, which are typically positive in GIST

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: The mass is described as hard with limited mobility, which is not typical of aggressive angiomyxoma, and the immunohistochemistry results do not support this diagnosis
